about.title: Personal Injury Help in Paradise, California
about.longDescription:
Paradise sits along Skyway, with Clark Road, Pearson Road, and Pentz Road carrying much of the town's daily traffic. In the most recent full year on record, Butte County logged 33 injury collisions in Paradise, leaving 45 people hurt and 3 people dead. Those numbers reflect public records, not any judgment about a particular street — they simply show that people in this small community do get hurt on the road, sometimes badly.

If you're one of them, sorting out medical bills, insurance calls, and lost work can feel like a second full-time job while you're still healing. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people in Paradise with an independent personal injury attorney — we are not a law firm, and we don't handle your case ourselves. We simply help you get in front of someone who can review what happened and explain your options. There's no cost to ask, and any attorney you're connected with works on contingency, meaning you owe nothing unless they recover money for you. You don't have to figure this out by yourself.

whyChoose.title: What You Should Know Before You Wait

items.title: The Clock Is Already Ticking
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity (like a public road agency) was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it helps to act sooner rather than later.

items.title: Being Partly at Fault Doesn't Shut the Door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you can still pursue compensation — it's just reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering Claims
items.desc: Unlike some states, California places no cap on non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in a typical injury case.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless they recover money for you. That means getting advice doesn't cost you anything out of pocket.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a crash in Paradise?
items.answer: In most California personal injury cases, you have two years from the date of the injury to file a lawsuit. If your injury involved a government entity or public property, that deadline can be much shorter — sometimes just six months — so it's worth checking your situation early.

items.question: What if I was partly to blame for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, so being partly at fault doesn't prevent you from recovering compensation. Your total recovery would simply be reduced by the percentage of fault assigned to you.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Paradise?
items.answer: Public collision records show that reported crashes in Paradise tend to peak on Fridays between 4 and 6 p.m., with higher collision counts along Skyway, Clark Road, Pearson Road, and Pentz Road. These are neutral counts from public records, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: No — California does not cap non-economic damages, such as pain and suffering, in standard personal injury cases. This differs from some other states that impose such limits.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No, connecting with an attorney through LawProactive is completely free, and we are not a law firm ourselves — we just help make the connection. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning you don't pay a fee unless they recover compensation for you.
